rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The five summary labels and counts sum to six and exactly match the six identified occurrences.

evaluation_limitations: No retrieved corpus passages or retrieval logs were supplied; corpus fidelity is therefore not scored.
This is a single-run evaluation; no dataset-level significance or comparative inference is calculated.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The new CVE was moved to the top of the queue and routed to the usual web-application remediation queue while the older database finding remained in place; the participant cited the fresh breach and the frequent injection-ticket pattern.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The segment contains comparative prioritization influenced by the recent breach (Recency) and initial categorization influenced by the frequently encountered web-application ticket pattern (Availability Frequency).

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: While cross-referencing assets, the participant saw a low-confidence privilege-escalation alert, relied on its historically benign resolution pattern, and did not consciously register the adjacent anomalous outbound-traffic entry.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The segment contains memory-based weighting of a familiar alert label (Availability Frequency) and failure to register a visually available cue during a competing task (Selective Attention Bias or Inattentional Blindness).

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The emergency change-window justification emphasized contract exposure, reputational fallout, and audit risk, even though the EPSS probability was moderate and comparable to findings handled in the normal weekend cycle.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly said that loss-oriented framing changed the felt urgency while the underlying EPSS score and disruption remained constant (Loss Framing).

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The participant scoped the patch ticket to the two hosts shown in the scanner's default view, treated that list as complete, and did not manually cross-check the inventory containing three additional affected hosts.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The available option set was implicitly limited to the scanner's default-view hosts, without checking the alternative inventory view (Exposure to limited alternatives).

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: prioritizing the new CVE over the older database finding
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Recent, vivid industry breach report primes a matching mental category, causing the newly disclosed CVE to be judged more urgent than an objectively higher-criticality older finding.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a near-neighbor label here; the finding identifies the recent breach as influential but does not use the hidden target label Recency or an approved exact equivalent.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The stated mechanism fully captures the fresh, emotionally salient breach being more accessible and shifting comparative urgency away from the older finding.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid participant quotes accurately support the recency-driven prioritization.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: routing the new CVE into a remediation queue
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: High historical frequency of web-app vulnerability tickets makes that category easiest to recall, causing miscategorization of a technically distinct authentication-bypass CVE.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Representativeness heuristic is related to categorization by resemblance but is not an approved equivalent of the hidden Availability Frequency target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding correctly captures miscategorization and underweighting of the advisory, but attributes the mechanism to prototype resemblance rather than the frequency/ease-of-recall of prior web-app tickets.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid participant quotes support the routing error and frequent-ticket pattern; the mechanism is over-specified as representativeness.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: disposition of the low-confidence privilege-escalation alert
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Frequent historical benign resolution of a specific SIEM alert label makes benign the easiest-recalled outcome, overriding specific diagnostic log evidence pointing to an active-threat category.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a broader near-neighbor label rather than an approved equivalent of the benchmark's Availability Frequency label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures frequent benign outcomes for this exact alert label overriding the unusual current log evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid quotes accurately distinguish historical alert-label resolution from the specific current alert cues.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_target_bias_label: Selective Attention Bias or Inattentional Blindness
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: failing to register anomalous outbound traffic while cross-referencing assets
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Narrow attentional focus on the asset-matching task causes failure to consciously register a visually available anomalous outbound traffic entry in the same dashboard panel.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Inattentional blindness is explicitly one of the hidden target's permitted equivalent formulations.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures failure to consciously register a visible cue while attention was engaged elsewhere.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The participant's uncertainty is preserved and the valid quote supports a missed visible dashboard cue.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: constructing the emergency change-window justification
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Urgency is constructed around potential losses rather than equivalent probability data, and the loss framing drives the urgency communicated to management.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Framing effect is a broader framing construct, not an approved exact equivalent of the hidden Loss Framing label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully identifies the loss-versus-neutral/gain presentation shift with invariant EPSS and disruption data.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid participant quotes explicitly compare the loss frame with an alternative frame and its effect on urgency.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: defining patch scope from the scanner default view
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The scanner's default-view host list is treated as the complete remediation option set without checking the asset inventory outside the default filter.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Automation bias and exposure to limited alternatives are distinct constructs, even though both can produce reliance on a default tool view.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures failure to cross-check and treating the visible list as complete, but explains it as automation overtrust rather than the option-set restriction itself.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid quotes accurately support the incomplete scoping decision and missed hosts.

The routing episode is correct, but the finding attributes the error to prototype resemblance rather than the hidden frequency-based availability mechanism.
It correctly identifies the historical-frequency mechanism and location, but uses a broader near-neighbor label instead of Availability Frequency.
It identifies the loss-frame mechanism and location but uses the broader Framing effect label rather than Loss Framing.
It correctly localizes the incomplete scope but supplies a different construct—automation overtrust—rather than exposure to limited alternatives.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: 4/4 positive reasoning segments detected at the recommended high_and_moderate threshold; no negative eligible segments were supplied.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: 1/6 hidden instances matched strictly (precision 0.1667, recall 0.1667, F1 0.1667) because most predictions used broader or different labels.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: 4/6 hidden mechanisms matched at the recommended threshold (precision 0.6667, recall 0.6667, F1 0.6667); two predictions were partial or different constructs.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were emitted, so candidate-tier inclusion has no marginal effect.
main_failure_modes: Near-neighbor labels were used instead of the benchmark's target labels.
Representativeness heuristic only partially matches the hidden frequency-based categorization mechanism.
Automation bias only partially matches exposure to limited alternatives.
Moderate-confidence findings are missed under a high-only threshold.
main_strengths: All six occurrences are localized to the correct four decision-point segments.
The output provides valid participant quotations and mechanism explanations.
The alert-attention and loss-framing findings are substantively strong; inattentional blindness is an approved equivalent label.
The RAG correctly discloses that no retrieval corpus was supplied.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment-level coverage when moderate confidence is included, but low strict ontology agreement. The mechanism-first score shows that most errors are taxonomy mismatches rather than failure to locate the relevant reasoning episodes, with residual substantive misses for the frequency-based routing instance and limited-alternatives instance.
